Subject: Clarify data use and deletion commitments for EdgeBank

Hi Sergio,

Quick question from procurement and legal: we need a clear, scannable statement for our security review that answers two things: 1) Does Redwood ever use EdgeBank customer content to further train or fine-tune models? 2) What are the retention timelines for request/response logs, debug snapshots, and backups, and where do those copies reside (region)?

We appreciate a short answer and any relevant artifacts (attestation, retention matrix, SOC2 excerpt).

Thanks,
Liam
Procurement, EdgeBank

EdgeBank Legal copied
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify data use and deletion commitments for EdgeBank

Liam — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: we do not use customer-provided inputs or request/response transcripts to train or fine-tune our public models unless a customer explicitly opts in. We can provide a signed attestation.

High-level bullets:
- Training: Customer content is excluded from Redwood model training and fine-tuning workflows by default.
- Telemetry: We may collect aggregated signal (latency, token distribution, categorical failure rates) for product quality; this data is non-identifiable and not used for model training.
- Opt-in: If a customer opts in to a research/quality program, that process is explicit, documented, and reversible; opt-in is required for any usage beyond the default exclusion.

Retention & residency (short):
- Request/response logs (short-term): retained for 30 days and stored in the customer region (US-east or US-west depending on your region setting).
- Debug snapshots & KV cache dumps (ephemeral dev ops): retained for up to 7 days by default; retained longer only under explicit debugging requests and with customer's approval.
- Backups & archives: encrypted backups for disaster recovery retained up to 90 days, stored in the configured region; billing/ledger records retained up to 13 months for invoicing where required.

I attached our non-training attestation, a retention matrix, and the SOC 2 section excerpt that callers typically ask for. Looping in Neha and Priyom for legal and ops detail.

Next step: if you want a signed attestation with legal signature and your PO referenced, tell me the contact and I will route.

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez

Hi Liam — adding a few technical/legal clarifications to the short statement Sergio shared.

Clarifications:
- "Do not use to train": This applies to all hosted and Dedicated deployments when the customer has selected the "No Training" option. For Redwood Private (customer-managed) deployments, Redwood has no access to application data by design.
- Aggregated telemetry: We aggregate metrics across customers and strip identifiers; this is used exclusively for platform stability and not for model parameter updates.
- Snapshots & backups: Snapshots taken for debugging are isolated to the specific cluster handling your tenancy; unless you approve extended retention, they are deleted on the stated schedule.
- Third parties: We do not share raw customer content with model vendors or third-party training partners. Any integration that requires data sharing is evaluated contractually and technically and will be explicitly disclosed.

Attached: suggested language for procurement (short paragraph) that you can paste into the contract. Happy to sign an attestation referencing EB-2026-0421.

Regards,

Liam — adding ops-level detail and a quick runbook in case you need to exercise deletion:

Operational details (how deletion works):
- Erase request flow: Submit an erase request via our portal (link below). Portal creates a ticket and triggers a coordinated purge across hot logs, cache, and index snapshots.
- Timeline: standard purge completes within 72 hours for hot stores; secondary snapshot/backups purged within the next 30 days subject to disaster-recovery hold overlap (we will annotate any holds).
- Proof: After purge completes, we provide a deletion confirmation with a trace id and a short audit record showing the stores purged.

Retention matrix (attached) maps each artifact to retention, default region, and whether it is involved in billing or auditing. We recommend including the 30-day request/response window and 7-day ephemeral debug window in contract language.

Portal / Evidence links: https://app.redwood.ai/records/EB-2026-0421 (we will upload the signed attestation here)

Regards,
